theme.title: From Tip to Buzzer
theme.subtitle: Teams, stars and stories from across basketball
theme.recap: The best numbers come from all over basketball history. Which answer surprised you most?

questions.prompt: Kobe Bryant scored 81 against Toronto in 2006. How many of those points came after halftime?
questions.note: 55 after halftime. The Lakers had trailed by 14 at the break before Kobe took over.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: with 55 points in the second half

funFacts.text: The Lakers trailed Toronto 63–49 at halftime.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Lakers trailed 63–49 at halftime

funFacts.text: Bryant played 42 minutes in the 81-point game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: saw Bryant play 42 minutes

funFacts.text: Bryant made seven three-pointers in that game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: including 7-of-13 on three-pointers

questions.prompt: How many home games did the 2010–11 Bulls win at the United Center?
questions.note: 36 wins at home against only five defeats.

funFacts.text: Chicago finished its regular season with only five home defeats.
The Bulls ended the season by winning every game they played during April.

questions.prompt: Before Damian Lillard's iconic 2014 series-winning three against Houston, how many seconds did Portland have left to inbound?
questions.context: Damian Lillard · Blazers vs Rockets · 2014 first round
questions.note: Just 0.9 seconds. Lillard caught the inbound and hit the buzzer-beater to eliminate Houston.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Chandler Parsons hit a reverse layup with 0.9 seconds remaining but the Rockets' hearts were broken when Damian Lillard

funFacts.text: Portland advanced to the second round for the first time since 2000.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Portland advanced to the second-round appearance for the first time since 2000

funFacts.text: John Stockton had hit the previous playoff-series-ending buzzer-beater.
